Rural Road is a Nopon Grand Prix Score Attack Course in . It takes place in Colony 9 in the afternoon. This course starts at the Mechon Wreckage Site and finishes at Cliff Lake.

Rose is an NPC in . She is a Tantalese who can be found at Anastatia's in the Kingdom of Tantal during The Home of the Soul. She is the daughter of Lazarus, who has been missing for eight years. According to Lazarus, Rose looked very similar to MOMO as a child.
Rudvic is an NPC in . Rudvic is an Urayan who can be found on a bench in Fonsa Myma's Entertainment District in the Kingdom of Uraya.
Rosaly is an NPC in . She is a Gormotti who can be found sitting on a bench above the Galad Residential Zone of Torigoth in the Gormott Province.
S-Missiles are back weapons for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Hyper Rail Cannon type Seidrs, green Pugiliths.
SHD-Gatlings are shoulder weapons for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Fal-swos.
SHD-Gravities are shoulder weapons for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Fal-swos.
SHD-Missiles are shoulder weapons for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Fal-swos.
SHD-Rays are shoulder weapons for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Fal-swos.
Rugged Raidrifles are ranged weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Assault Rifles. They can be obtained from the Shop Terminal in Armory Alley for 15,000 Credits.
Rugged Deadsights are ranged weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Sniper Rifles. They can be obtained from the Shop Terminal in Armory Alley for 18,000 Credits.
Rugged Deadsights II are ranged weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Sniper Rifles. They can be obtained from the Shop Terminal in Armory Alley for 18,000 Credits.
Rugged Sidearms are ranged weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Dual Guns. They can be obtained from the Shop Terminal in Armory Alley for 16,500 Credits.
Rurui (Japanese: , Iruiru) is an NPC in . Rurui is a Nopon who can be found at Argentum Bazaar in the Argentum Trade Guild's Goldmouth. Rurui runs a shop called Whiteside Salvaging.

Rumtumtum is an NPC in . Rumtumtum is a Nopon who can be found at Rumbletum Canteen in the Argentum Trade Guild's Goldmouth. Rumtumtum runs a shop called Rumbletum Canteen specialized in Staple Foods.

Satorl Marsh (Japanese: , Rinkō no ji Zatōru, alternatively Land of Phosphorescent Sator; English dub: ) is one of several areas visited by the party in . The party must proceed through the marshes, up Bionis' waist and lower back, in order to get to the upper areas of Bionis. Due to its location at the hip of the Bionis, the Homs colony of Colony 6 has a road that directly leads to the marsh. Satorl Marsh is an area with a permanent fog and a resilient fauna. At night, the released ether of the swamp creates a beautiful shimmer. It possesses High Entia and Giant ruins. It does not possess any permanent settlements. Its only inhabitants are a caravan of Nopon traders and Zazadan, another Nop
The Satorl Marsh Collection is a portion of the Collectopaedia in Xenoblade Chronicles.

Scarlet Ladybirds (Japanese: , Kurenaitentou) are collectables in . They can be found in Makna Forest. According to their description, they are bright red ladybirds and a decent dye is made from their defensive secretions.

Schorl Mushrooms (Japanese: , Torumarindake) are collectables in . They can be found in Makna Forest. According to their description, they look like cold green mushrooms but they are actually succulent and tasty.
This page is a list of all the Unique Monsters in Satorl Marsh.

Scout Hodes (Japanese: , Sukauto Fūdi) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Hode family, and can be found at level 30 beside the Windmill Pavilion in Makna Forest. They can drop the Hode Planks needed for Bridge Repair and Colony 6 Reconstruction.

Sea Berries (Japanese: , Sī Berī) are collectables in . They can be found in the Eryth Sea and Colony 6. According to their description, they are enormous white flowers that remind someone of a snowy scene when open. Three are required for Colony 6 Reconstruction. In , they can be purchased from the Nopon Archsage in Time Attack for 8,100 Noponstones.

Scarlen (Japanese: , Segāru) is a High Entia in Xenoblade Chronicles. He can be found in Alcamoth. He offers a series of quests concerning the resolution of a love triangle involving him and two female High Entia, Ricoth and Rozeal. This love triangle is the subject of some negative gossip among the citizens of Alcamoth, who view Scarlen in a negative light for what they perceive as his insincerity regarding his two female friends, assuming him to be playing them.
Satata (Japanese: , Tatsu) is a Nopon in . He can be found first in the Refugee Camp on Bionis' Leg, then north of the Reconstruction HQ in Colony 6, past the first shop.

The Sani Telethia (Japanese: , Sanī Tereshia), or Sunny Telethia, is a Boss in . It is Alvis' Telethia, appearing to be a unique specimen not resembling the more common Phoenix, Licorne, Drakos or Gigas types of Telethia.
Sea Frogs (Japanese: , Shinrakāsu) are collectables in . They can be found in the Eryth Sea. According to their description, they reside in warm climes and they have a voracious appetite for fish.
Search Quest 1 (Japanese: , Osagashi Kuesuto 1) is a quest in . It can be received from a Homs in the Central Plaza of Colony 9.

Sarsaparillas (Japanese: , Sarusaperira) are collectables in . They can be found in Bionis' Interior. According to their description, it is a very hot vegetable and not even the best cook on Bionis can make it taste good.
Search Quest 3 (Japanese: , Osagashi Kuesuto 3) is a quest in . It can be received from a Homs near the center area of the Commercial District of Colony 9.
Search Quest 2 (Japanese: , Osagashi Kuesuto 2) is a quest in . It can be received from a Nopon southeast of the Residential District of Colony 9.
Search Quest 4 (Japanese: , Osagashi Kuesuto 4) is a quest in . It can be received from a Homs southwest of the Residential District in Colony 9.

This quest will expire after the decision to move to Colony 6. Save the Girl! (Japanese: , Josei wo Tasukero) is a Timed Surprise Quest in . It is received after Sharla has joined the party and they travel to the waterfall in the southeast area of Gaur Plain on Bionis' Leg.

Secret Elixir Ingredients (Japanese: , Hiyaku no Zairyō Atsume) is a quest in . It can be received from Lupa at the Archaeology Centre in Frontier Village. It is automatically triggered once Kind Lupa's Grampypon has been accepted.

Secret Ingredient Hunt (Japanese: , Himitsu no Zairyō Atsume) is a quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Bana after completing Pollen Orb Ingredients. He can be found in the southeast area of the Central Plaza in Frontier Village. Gadada must be spoken to to begin this quest. If Melia is in the active party, she will comment.

Secret Innovation (Japanese: , Himitsu no Gijutsukakushin) is a quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Rasha after completing Pollen Orb Ingredients. She can be found in the Central Plaza of Frontier Village, first lying on the southeast border of Sacred Altar's pool then at the Armour Shop. If Sharla is in the active party, she will comment.

Secret Mission (Japanese: , Gokuhi no Ninmu) is a quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Daza in the Watchpoint Junction in the outskirts of Colony 6, or at the Hope Farm Shop once the Reconstruction has started. If Shulk is in the active party, he will comment. The Top-Secret Data received from this quest is needed in order to complete Find the Kingpin in Frontier Village, but it is possible to accept these quests in either order.

Scarlet Crawler (Japanese: , Hiirokemushi) are collectables in . They can be found in Mechonis Field and Colony 6. According to their description, they are caterpillars of delicate red with fine hairs that are sharp like needles.

The Scrap Driver (Japanese: , Jankubankā) is a weapon in . It is a gunlance wielded by Reyn. It is Reyn's initial equipment, made for him by Shulk, and cannot be acquired from any other source, although can be sold. Reyn first uses it in-game to stop a Krabble from attacking Shulk at the Mechon Wreckage Site in Colony 9. After the battle, he comments that it is 'excellent'.

Scissor Bugs (Japanese: , Tachibasamimushi) are collectables in . They can be found in Agniratha and Colony 6. According to their description, they have giant sets of pincers that they lubricate with secretions.

The Satorl Guardian (Japanese: , Zatōru no Shugosha) is a quest exclusive boss in . It is a member of the Ansel family, and it is fought at level 28 at the Sororal Statues in Satorl Marsh after performing the High Entia coming-of-age ceremony at the Adulthood Emblem during the story quest The Ancient Ceremony. Like most story quest bosses, the Satorl Guardian drops no treasure.

Satorl Flamiis (Japanese: , Zatōru Furamī) are enemies in . They are members of the Flamii family, and can be found at level 22 in the Kelsher Wetland of Satorl Marsh anytime but with no fog. They are very similar to Marsh Flamiis. Both share the Kick Rush and Binding Screech Arts. They attack on sight as well as if another of its kind is attacked. They can drop the Twin Flamii Eggs needed for Preventing Starvation.
Sakura Drones are Mechonis Drones in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be bought at the Machina Refuge.
School Shoes are medium feet armour in Xenoblade Chronicles.

※ After this quest is completed, Dulland may offer quest A Flower for a Rose and Elior may offer quest Supplies for Satorl. Securing Provision (Japanese: , Shokuryō Kakuho) is a quest in . It can be received from Dulland on the Junks landed close to the Reconstruction HQ in Colony 6. If Melia is in the active party, she will comment.

Satata's Younger Brother (Japanese: , Tatsu no Otōto) is a quest in . It can be received from Satata in Colony 6. Completing this quest will unlock Rest in Peace. If Shulk is in the active party, he will comment.
Save the Machina! (Japanese: , Dōhō wo Sukue) is a quest in . It can be received from Voltak inside the Junks on the Fallen Arm. If Sharla is in the active party, she will comment.
The Saint Rod (Japanese: , Seintoroddo) is a weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a staff and is usable by Melia.

Scheduled Inspection (Japanese: , Jūnen ni Ichido no Teikikensa) is a quest in . It can be received from Xekit at the Ether Light of the Hidden Machina Village on the Fallen Arm. If Fiora is in the active party, she will comment.
Satellite Shots (Japanese: , Sateraitoshotto) are weapons in . They are rifles that can be wielded by Sharla. They can be acquired as a quest reward.
The Search Sniper (Japanese: , Sāchisunaipu) is a weapon in . It is one of Sharla's ether rifles. It can be purchased in Colony 6 for 7,600 Gold.
Seacle Gloves are light arms armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are only equippable by Alvis during the short period of time he joins the party in Makna Forest.
The Seacle Shoes are light feet armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are only equippable by Alvis during the short period of time he teams up with Shulk in Makna Forest.

The Seacle Cap (Japanese: , Shīkuru Kyappu) is light head armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is exclusive to Alvis. It is worn by him during the short time he teams up with Shulk in Makna Forest, and cannot be removed or sold.
The Seacle Bottoms are light legs armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are only equippable by Alvis during the short period of time he teams up with Shulk in Makna Forest.
The Seacle Top is light torso armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is only equippable by Alvis during the short period of time he teams up with Shulk in Makna Forest.

Secret Areas (Japanese: , hikyō, Secret/Unexplored Region) are discoverable Landmarks in the . Secret Areas are always landmarks, making them available for Skip Travel after they are found. They are often hidden away or otherwise difficult to find. Many secret areas offer scenic views or other special points of interest, commonly quest-related. In , there are not Landmarks named Secret Areas, however Scenic Viewpoints and Unexplored Territories are discoverable places similar to Secret Areas. Despite their names in the English versions, they are Landmarks and not Areas.

Sap Cave (Japanese: , Jueki no Horaana) is a location in . It is located in Makna Forest, near the pool from the south of Contaminated Area. During Mystery of Makna Ruins 3, the party is asked to get three Algora Saps from this location. The entrance to the cave is behind a large Makna Brog.
Save the Worker (Japanese: , Sagyōin wo Kyūjoseyo) is a Story Quest in . It is received automatically at the Whitewing Palace after the story events upon arrival at Alcamoth.

The Sealed Chamber (Japanese: , Fūin no Ma) is a landmark in . It is located on the ground floor of the High Entia Tomb, a short way east of the entrance to the tomb, Tomb Approach. There is a locked door here which can only be opened by a descendant of the High Entia Ancestors, and it leads to the Hall of Spirits. However, if someone without the blood of the ancestors attempts to open the door, the floor will open, and the intruders will fall to the Tomb Robber Pool a floor below.

The Second Treasury (Japanese: , Dai-2 Hōmotsuko) is a location in . It is located in the second basement floor of the High Entia Tomb. The Second Treasury is reachable through a passage that does not appear on the map and connects the room to the hole in the north wall of the corridor between the Valley of Emperors and the Tower of Trials - Bridge. As its name suggests it contains the High Entia Treasure. The Calm Anzabi may appear and attack the party, from a hole in the ceiling, a few seconds after entering the room.

Secret Research (Japanese: , Himitsu no Kenkyūjo) is a quest in . It can be received from Teelan at the Ether Plant at Eryth Sea after the events at the Mechonis Core and after completing The Missing Boy. If Fiora is in the active party, she will comment. The High Entia Emblem is required to access the Telethia Laboratory, which can be found east of the Ceremony Hall landmark in the High Entia Tomb. The Furious Jozan is also guarding the laboratory.

Say Sorry (Japanese: , Kuiaratame mo) is one of Riki's physical arts in . If the enemy is suffering from any debuffs, this art's damage is increased by 100% times the number of debuffs, but the debuffs are removed from the enemy. For example, if the enemy has two debuffs, the damage will be tripled.

The Second Lung (Japanese: , Dai 2 Hai Naibu) is a location in . It is located in the Bionis' Interior. Three Unique Monsters can be found here, in addition to three spawn points capable of giving Black Liver Beans and a rare Electric Ether deposit. The fastest way to access it is to Skip Travel to the Terminal Nerve Tower, to head west and drop down, then to continue on the blue coloured path to reach the Second Lung.
Second Gear (Japanese: , Sekando Gia) is one of Fiora's Ether support arts in . When activated, it increases her physical arts damage by 50% for five seconds.

Satorl Volffs are enemies in . They are members of the Volff family, and can be found at level 24 around most of eastern Satorl Marsh in the daytime, near the Barren Moor and the Glowing Obelisk. They can drop the Fancy Volff Hides needed for Making Camp.

Sardis (Japanese: , Sādi) are a family of aquatic enemies in and . Sardis are fish-like creatures found outside Colony 9, on Bionis' Leg, and in Makna Forest. They are very similar to, and may be related to Piranhax.

Scout Entia (Japanese: , Sukauto Entā) are two story exclusive enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are High Entia, and are fought in Alcamoth once, when the party is attacked in their quarters by a group of assassins of the Bionite Order.

The Satisfied Gogol (Japanese: , Hōman no Gogōru) is a quest exclusive enemy in . It is a member of the Gogol family, and can be found at level 96 at the Trader's Stopover near Heavenly Window in Tephra Cave. The Satisfied Gogol only appear during the Securing Provisions quest, guarding the required Trader's Spare Key. It can drop Gogol Horns, which are needed for both A Token of Friendship and Colony 6 Reconstruction.

This quest will expire upon the events at the end of Mechonis Field. Secure Dolgan Outpost (Japanese: , Dorugan Kanshisai Seiatsu) is a Timed Surprise Quest in . It can be received in Sword Valley. The party must defeat the Prudent Purson at Dolgan Outpost. This is a Timed Quest and will become unavailable after reaching the end of Mechonis Field.

This quest will expire upon the events at the end of Mechonis Field. Secure Enalda Control Base (Japanese: , Enaruda Kanri Kichi Seiatsu) is a Timed Surprise Quest in . It can be received in Sword Valley. The party must defeat the Tranquil Morax at the Enalda Control Base. This is a Timed Quest and will become unavailable after reaching the end of Mechonis Field.

This quest will expire upon the events at the end of Mechonis Field. Secure the Radio Tower (Japanese: , Denpatō Butai Chin'atsu) is a Timed Surprise Quest in . It can be received in Sword Valley. The party must defeat the Lightning Ronove, who is in the area around the Radio Tower. It is a Timed Quest and will become unavailable after reaching the end of Mechonis Field.

Satorl Vang (Japanese: , Zatōru Vanpu) are enemies in . They are members of the Vang family, and can be found at levels 21-24 in the Satorl Marsh. A group of them can be found in the cave south of the Nopon Merchant Camp. They can drop the Vang Milk Teeth needed for Let's Make Fillings!.
Satorl Rhoguls are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Rhogul family, and can be found at levels 84-85 in Satorl Marsh at night, replacing the Mist Rhoguls seen during the day.

Scout Unit Prototypes (Japanese: , Teisatsu-gata: PROTO) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Mechon, and can be found at level 53 on the Fallen Arm near the Giant Mechon Debris and on Digit 5 Beach. They are the only source of Dated Cranks, which are needed for Odd Smoke - Resolution.

__FORCETOC__ Secondo Novas (Japanese: , Sekondo Nova) are story exclusive enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Nebula family, and can be found at level 72 in Bionis' Interior only during the boss battle with Lorithia occurring into Bionis' heart. Although they do not respawn, several of them may be summoned during the course of the battle.

Saturn (Japanese: , Kioku Kūkan - Dosei) is a landmark in . It is located in Memory Space, and is one of the final locations in the game. The only enemy found here is Spirit - Mumkhar, and there is a transporter to Jupiter.

The Secret Nopon Elixir is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. Collecting the ingredients to make it is the objective of Secret Elixir Ingredients. It must be delivered to Satata in Colony 6 to complete Kind Lupa's Grampypon.

Sauros (Japanese: , Saurā) are large dinosaur-like enemies in the . They are structurally similar to Dragons, Dragues, and Draiguls. Sauros' appearance changes between games; in they have fewer stripes and smaller spines than in and a facial structure closer to a tyrannosaurus rex.
Screw Edge (Japanese: , Sukuryū Ejji) is one of Fiora's early game physical arts in . It may inflict Break on an enemy.

Samurai Gunner (known as Samurai Gun in the Japanese version) is a Class featured in Xenoblade Chronicles X. This class provides bonuses to HP and melee attack. It is one of two classes that can be leveled up from Striker and can be leveled up to Duelist. The playable characters of this class include Gwin, whereas Frye's class is an Alternative Samurai Gunner. Samurai Gunner has two Skill slots.
Screamer is a Debuff Battle Art in . It inflicts Sleep on enemies.
The Sealed Package is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is received from Betty during The Plan - Preparation, and must be delivered to Sesame to complete the quest.

Scarlen's Letter is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is received from Scarlen during one of two quests. In Together Forever the letter is to be delivered to Rozeal. In I Love You No Matter What it is to be delivered to Ricoth. Only one of these quests will be offered, depending on the choice made in How Do I Feel?.
Secondary Speed is one of Hope's two Signature Arts in . It is learned by completing A False Hope.

Scirpos (Japanese: , Shirunea) are spider-like creatures in Xenoblade Chronicles X. In general, red scirpos tend to be aggressive hunters, while blue and pink scirpos are docile scavengers. They can be found in Primordia, Noctilum, Oblivia, and Sylvalum.

Sea Forfexes (Japanese: , Shī Pagurusu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Forfex family, and can be found at level 11-12 or level 19-20 on the coasts of Primordia. Five must be defeated to complete The Celeste Three.

The Seaswept Base (Japanese: , Fūha no Yōsai) is an area in . It is located in Primordia, near Seaswept Rise and Seaswept Ridge. It is a Prone base, as well as where Cross, Elma, and Lin first meet Tatsu. FN Site 119 is located near the northern side of the base.
The Seaswept Ridge (Japanese: , Fūha no Tōge) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Primordia, near Seaswept Base, southwest of South Janpath BC, and east of New Los Angeles.

Sayram Northeast Plain (Japanese: , Sairamu-ko no Hokutō Heigen) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Primordia, northwest of Sickle Rock Rise and northeast of Sayram Lake. Dieter, the Epicure may run through Sayram Northeast Plain while on its patrol route.
Saltats (Japanese: , Sarutāto) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are large bird-like creatures with horn-shaped heads similar to Liceors.
Satie (Japanese: , Sati) is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She can be found near the East Gate in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles during the day.

Sayram Lake (Japanese: , Sairamu-ko) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Primordia, to the north of West Gate Plain and south of the Grieving Plains. The Beasts' Lair is situated under an overhang on the northeast shore, and the Sayram Lake BC is here.
The Sapphire Carpet (Japanese: , Seigyoku Jūtan) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a pass located in Noctilum, west of Yagami's Vista and northeast of Rust Lake.
The Sapphire Table (Japanese: , Seigyoku Kōgen) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Noctilum, northeast of Sapphire Carpet and Yagami's Vista and southwest of the Garden Spring.

The Sailing Grex (Japanese: , Seiru Rupusu) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Grex and can be found at level 16 on Biahno Grassland in Primordia. It only appears during the quest A Day in the Life. It is accompanied by a horde of six Fighter Grexes.
The Sayram Lake BC (Japanese: , Sairamu-ko BC) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a BLADE base camp located in Primordia, on the shore of Sayram Lake.

The Seabird's Beak (Japanese: , Umidori no Kuchibashi) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is the first and southernmost location in Sylvalum, and also Sylvalum's only beach. The FN Site 403 is located here, as is the Seabird's Beak BC.

Sand Forfexes (Japanese: , Sando Pagurusu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Forfex family, and can be found at level 19-20 in Oblivia, to the West of the Barbarich Desert.

Sapphire Forfexes (Japanese: , Safaia Pagurusu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Forfex family, and can be found at level 11-14 at Seabird's Beak in Sylvalum. Two must be defeated to complete Bottoms Up.
Sanctuary Progen (Japanese: , Sankuchuari Ekuusu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Progen and can be found at level 52 at Twin Hammers in Noctilum.

Sea Whisper Valley (Japanese: , Shiosai no Tani, Sea Roar Valley) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Oblivia, northeast of East Ibra Ravine and east of Victory Rock. It leads to Jair Fortress, and is filled with mid-level Ganglion. The large rock in the center of the valley has several collectibles on top, and a narrow passageway runs through it.

Scarlet Levitath (Japanese: , Sukāretto Rukiora) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Levitath family, and can be found at level 44-45 at Rust Lake or at level 49-50 at Upper Hushflood in Noctilum at night.
Sand Caro (Japanese: , Sando Nokkusu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Caro family and can be found at level 38-40 in Sylvalum, near FN Site 416 or FN Site 418.
Scourer Grexes (Japanese: , Kurīnā Rupusu, Cleaner Lupus) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Grex family, and can be found at level 31-40 in Oblivia, north of FN Site 317.

Scout Puges (Japanese: , Sukauto Berude) are three Story and Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Puge machines, Ganglion's human size robots, and can be found at level 28 at the NLA Primary Defense Line in Primordia during Chapter 8. Three of them must be defeated in the first wave of Ganglion attacks.
Scandium Petramands (Japanese: , Sukanjiumu Aranea) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Petramand family and can be found at level 47 near FN Site 216 in Noctilum.

Sarona (Japanese: , Sarona) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She can be found in the Administrative District, near the BLADE Barracks between BLADE Concourse and the East Gate, along with Inisae. She is a member of the Prospectors Division. She can be found at Talon Rock Second Terrane then at Third Terrane in Primordia during Close Encounters.
Sea Xiphias (Japanese: , Shī Rumederu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Xiphias family, and can be found at level 21-30 at Northpointe Cove in Primordia.
Savanna Adseculas (Japanese: , Saban'na Apisu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Adsecula family, and can be found at level 25-26 at Unicorn Rock in Primordia.

Sapphire Visigels (Japanese: , Safaia Narukī) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Visigel family, and can be found at level 51-53 on the eastern side of the land strip bisecting Lake Ciel or at level 59-60 in Sylvalum and Sylvalum Waters.

The Scholes Battlegrounds (Japanese: , Sukōruzu Kosenjō-ato) are an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Cauldros, southwest of the Emerian Battlegrounds and directly north of the path to Sylvalum. The Drongo Caravan is located north of here.
The Samuel Incline (Japanese: , Samyueru Kōbai) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Sylvalum, northeast of Badr Basin.

Schneider, the Cliffpercher (, Gaisai no Shunaidā) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Forfex family. It can be found at level 10 west of FN Site 212 in Noctilum. It is hidden on one of the rocks lodged into the waterfall, immediately below a cluster of Violet Forfex. The Tyrant emerges once closely approached. Defeating it is required to complete the eponymous Basic Mission Schneider, the Cliffpercher.
Satsu is an NPC in . He is a Nopon and can be found in the Whale's Nostril in Noctilum. He is met during the mission The Ties That Bind. He is Tatsu's brother.
Samanya is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She can be found in the Central Industrial District of New Los Angeles during the day.

Sandy Sabulas (Japanese: , Sandī Sabueru) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Sabula family, and can be found at level 42-44 at South Silent Sandsea and North Silent Sandsea in Sylvalum.

Sarcosuchus, the Iron-Eater (, Tekkui no Sarukosukusu) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Dilus family, and rather larger than the surrounding Diluses. It can be found at level 39 at Rust Lake in Noctilum. It leaps out from the lake when its area is approached. Defeating it is required to complete the eponymous Basic Mission Sarcosuchus, the Iron-Eater and to complete segment recon. It must be defeated for Squad Mission No.15.

Seabound Coil Tree (Japanese: , Shikai Daimakigi) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a large tree located in Noctilum, visually identical to the Skybound Coil Tree. There are no enemies here, but Yoyotsu and Kan'tonam are here during Missing in Action and Lone Survivors respectively.

Sato Headwater (Japanese: , Sato Suigen) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a cave located in Noctilum, north of FN Site 205, and is inhabited only by Scintimures, which are not initially visible. It is inaccessable to Skells and contains two Treasure Boxes, water, and a great mass of branches.

Scabland Fortress (Japanese: , Dorairando Gankutsu Yōsai, Dryland Cave Fort) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Ganglion base located in Oblivia, west of the Leaning Ring. The FN Site 307 is located on the lower tier of the fortress. The Internment Camp Key and Dancer's Clothes must be found here during Prone Sweet Prone and Quegga's Gift respectively.
Samuel Incline BC (Japanese: , Samyueru Kōbai BC) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a BLADE base camp located in Sylvalum.

Sanelac Pearls (Japanese: , Saneraku Shinju) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Primordia, in particular around Talon Rock Second Terrane or at the Beasts' Lair. Four are required for the Basic Mission Partners in Pearls. fr:Perle sanelac
Sand Cucumbers (Japanese: , Kurippanako) are rare collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Oblivia.
Sandstone Etchings (Japanese: , Sagan no Sekiban) are rare collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Oblivia. Eight are required for the basic mission A History Lesson.

Scales of Justice (Japanese: , Zettaishugi no Tenbin) are prime collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in southern Noctilum, around Rustpool Banks and Old Dragontail Tree. Three of them are needed for Scaling Up.
]] The Samaarians (Japanese: , Samāru; English dub: ) are a mysterious race in .
Sea Anenome Platters (Japanese: , Anemoni-kai no Sara) are rare collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Noctilum. Three are required for the Basic Mission The Fail Parade.
Savage Claws (Japanese: , Mādāneiru) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Cauldros.

Savage Sketches (Japanese: , Suketchi Monsutā) are prime collectibles in . They appear rarely on the east side of Cauldros around the Kw'arah Cloister, FN Site 514, and FN Site 515, as well as in Cauldros Waters east of this area. Six are needed for the level 5 Mechanical Basic Mission Off the Record in the original version and Off the Record (biological) in the .
Samarium Petramands (Japanese: , Samariumu Aranea) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Petramands and can be found at level 35-36 near the Abandoned Bivouac in Cauldros.

The Secluded Lava Lake (Japanese: , Yōganko no Dōkutsu) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a cave whose entrance is located near FN Site 401 in Sylvalum. There are a great many hidden Sacrifoles in this cave. Phina can be found here during Predator and Prey, as can Professor B during Professorial.

Sandsprint Slope (Japanese: , Sunahashiri no Saka) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a natural passageway located in Sylvalum, north of the left body of water in Lake Ciel and south of the South Cinderdunes. It must be visited during Soldier of the Harriers.
Sapara, the Laconic (Japanese: , Seijaku no Sapara) is a Tyrant in . It is a member of the Saltat family. It can rarely be found at level 22 west of Unicorn Rock in Primordia.
The Sector Security Shrad (Japanese: , Shūhen Keigoyō Zuttā) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Shrad Ganglion machine. It can be found at level 46 at Boxtrap Checkpoint in Cauldros.
Saltat Horns are common in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Saltats. One of them is needed to complete the related Basic Mission Indigen Investigation. fr:Corne de Saltats

Secret Germivores (Japanese: , Haido Burōsu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Germivore family, and can be found at level 31-32 at Hilal Meadow near Hilal Stronghold in Sylvalum.
Sea Balaenas (Japanese: , Shī Baraena) are enemies in . They are members of the Balaena family, and can be found at level 41-50 in Primordia near FN Site 121.
Sapphire Horns are materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Xiphias in Primordia or Noctilum, or traded for 42 Reward Tickets. Three are needed for Forbidden Love.
Sara-Ariel is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She can be found at the Division Drive in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles. She is a member of the Harriers division.
Secondary Accelerator is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Mastermind at rank 10. Cross and Yelv can use this skill.
Scirpo Silks are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Scirpos. One is needed for the related mission The Next Big Thing.

The Scout Galdr (Japanese: , Sukauto Garudora) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Galdr machine, and can be found at level 54 at Decapotamon in Noctilum. Defeating it is required during Rapid Misfire.

Scout Qmoevas (Japanese: , Sukauto Kumūba) are two Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Qmoeva machines, and can be found at level 50 at Decapotamon in Noctilum. Defeating them is required during Rapid Misfire.

San'luarb (Japanese: , San'eibu) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is an Orphean who can be found at the Integrated Production Plant in the Industrial District of New Los Angeles in the daytime after No-show Nen'celeg is completed. During the quest Orphean Pluck, he tries to work with Non'barac to install Data Probes so they don't have to rely on other species for a steady supply of Miranium but it only puts Non'barac in danger. While he initially acted as the leader of the duo, the roles have reversed after Non'barac returns and he now mainly focuses on crafting components while Non'barac handles the negotiating. San'luarb tried pitching the idea of making replacement mimeosome parts

The Sazon Caladar (Japanese: , De Sazon) is a Mission Exclusive Secondary Boss in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is the Caladar Skell piloted by De Sazon, fought at level 40 at the North Silent Sandsea in Sylvalum during Leaving the Nest.
Sandman is a Soul Voice in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is triggered when a character puts an enemy to sleep.
Search Request is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from a Male BLADE and the primary destination is Primordia. It is a request to retrieve a runaway Labrador.
Sajif Scoppio (Japanese: , Sajifu Sukoppio) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is a Tree Clan Prone and can be found at the Starboard of the Ma-non Ship in New Los Angeles during the day.
Scintimure Fat is a rare material in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Scintimures.

The Sapphire Ring is an Important Item in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is obtained after defeating the Stray Potamus at Lake Ciel. Bringing the Sapphire Ring to Nio at Dopang Caravan will make Hair Apparent available. It is possible to obtain a second Sapphire Ring by defeating the Stray Potamus after completing Hair Apparent.
Securing Lan'cord is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is received automatically from Eleonora on the BLADE Concourse during Murderess's Affinity Mission The Little Rich Girl.
Scaling Up is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from a physicist to obtain Scales of Justice.
Scouting in Secret is a Basic Mission in . It is a request from Stella and the primary destination is the Administrative District.
Search Support Request is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from Sherry and the primary destination is the Administrative District.

Securing Our Safety is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from Ajoa and the primary destination is the Residential District. This Basic Mission leads into Water Woes, though it does not have to be accepted to start Water Woes.

Salvage Tickets are Consumable Items in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be received as Division Rewards for Division activities. They can be used to repair a Skell which is wrecked after its insurance expires.
Salsa Salvo is L's fourth Heart-to-Heart in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It occurs between L and Cross in front of the NLA Food building in the Commercial District of New Los Angeles.

Scirpo Cyanide Sacs are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Scirpos with blue-green acid sacs, or for 36 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are components in all Melee: Shock and M-Auto.SHOCK augments.

Scirpo Sulfuric Acid Sacs are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Scirpos with pink acid sacs, or for 54 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are components in all SpecUp.FUEL-OD augments.
Scirpo Malic Acid Sacs are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Scirpos that have red acid sacs.
Scorching Giant Cells are unique materials in . They can be obtained from Gularth.
The School Blazer is a casual full body armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It shares its appearance with the College Blazer.
Saltat A is a Holofigure in . It depicts a red saltat variant with a golden belly. It can be obtained from Sapara, the Laconic in Primordia.
Saltat B is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a red saltat variant with a green belly with hollows. It can be obtained from Aria, the Zauberflöte in Noctilum.
Saltat C is a Holofigure in . It depicts a red saltat variant with a blue belly. It can be obtained from Zdenka, the Raucous in Primordia.
Saltat D is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a red saltat variant with a white belly. It can be obtained from Jarosch, the Sensational in Noctilum.
Saltat E is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a blue saltat variant with a golden belly. It can be obtained from Wenzel, the Inebriated in Oblivia.
Saltat F is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a blue saltat variant with a green bell with hollows. It can be obtained from Zorn, the Wanderer in Cauldros.
Saltat G is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a blue saltat variant with a blue belly. It can be obtained from Rolf, the Sonorous in Oblivia.
